domain: normalized Boolean CNF of maximum clause width <=3

theorem.statement: For every fixed constant s>=1, every nonempty width<=3 CNF F with surplus sigma(F)=s admits a deterministic polynomial-time satisfiability-preserving transition that strictly decreases the number of variables.
algorithm: Compute p(v), q(v) for every variable.
If some v satisfies p(v)q(v)<=p(v)+q(v), apply exact Davis-Putnam elimination to v (R44AT).
Otherwise compute a nonempty surplus witness V with |Gamma(V)|-|V|=s using the inherited polynomial surplus-witness algorithm.
Because no variable satisfies the R44AT inequality, every variable has total degree at least 5.
Width<=3 gives sum_{v in V} d(v) <= 3|Gamma(V)| = 3(|V|+s), while the no-R44AT condition gives sum_{v in V} d(v) >=5|V|. Hence |V|<=floor(3s/2).
Eliminate all variables in V by ordinary exact Davis-Putnam elimination in a fixed deterministic order.

complexity.cheap_case: R44AT is polynomial with nonincreasing clause count.
complexity.bounded_witness_case: Let M_i be the clause count after i eliminations. A crude bound is M_{i+1}<=M_i+M_i^2<=2M_i^2. After k<=floor(3s/2) eliminations, M_k<=2^(2^k-1) m^(2^k). For fixed s, k and 2^k are constants, so state and charged work are polynomial in the original input size.
complexity.uniformity_ceiling: The polynomial exponent depends on s. This is not a uniform polynomial bound when s grows with the input.

exactness.semantics: Each Davis-Putnam elimination is exact existential projection of the eliminated variable and preserves satisfiability.
exactness.strict_progress: At least one variable is eliminated; in the bounded-witness case every variable in nonempty V is eliminated.
exactness.terminality: NOT_CLAIMED. This is a one-step theorem, not a complete decision algorithm.

consequences: R44BA's sigma<=2 theorem is subsumed at the existence-of-one-step level, though R44BA has much cheaper transitions.
The sigma=3 layer cannot be a width-3 fixed-point layer: if no cheap R44AT variable exists, a surplus witness has at most 4 variables and can be eliminated with fixed polynomial overhead.
More generally, no fixed constant surplus level s can by itself form an irreducible width-3 obstruction family against exact polynomial one-step progress.
Any obstruction family to this meta-theorem's fixed-s strategy must have surplus unbounded along the family or leave the width<=3 domain after the transition.

next_admissible_math.question: Can the bounded-witness elimination step be replaced by a uniform exact transition whose polynomial exponent is independent of sigma(F), or can one prove a barrier for one precisely specified such compression?
forbidden_shortcuts: treat s as a hidden constant
increase a fixed DP budget under a new name
hide exponential projection in a terminal evaluator
claim fixed-parameter or XP behavior as ordinary polynomial time
